title.narrative: Department for Work and Pensions Annual Report and Accounts 2023-2024

description.narrative: This Annual Report and Account sets out the activities of the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) over the 2023 to 2024 financial year. DWP reported on ODA spend separately in Statistics on International Development: final UK ODA spend 2023

title.narrative: UK Government Statistics on International Development: final UK ODA spend 2023

description.narrative: This publication outlines UK Official Development Assistance (ODA) spend for January to December 2023, including DWP's ODA-eligible spend. DWP published a separate Annual Report and Account which sets out the activities of the Department over the 2023 to 2024 financial year.

title.narrative: The UK government’s strategy for international development

description.narrative: ODA spend in the Department for Work and Pensions is in scope of the UK Government's broader strategy for international development. DWP's ODA-eligible multilateral spend contributes to deepening cooperation with international organisations (paragraph 1) and DWP's ODA-eligible in-donor spend contributes to meeting the UK's international obligations to protect refugees and people seeking asylum (paragraph 22).

title.narrative: Afghanistan resettlement and immigration policy statement

description.narrative:
All DWP in-donor refugee costs (IDRC) are paid to individuals where the Home Office has granted them an eligible immigration status with recourse to public funds and who have then gone on to claim DWP public funds benefits. For this reason, DWP does not pre-allocate IDRC, or have an allocation policy, as it depends on the number of visas granted by the Home Office per scheme and subsequently, of these, the number of people who go on to claim DWP public funds benefits.
The Home Office’s Afghan Resettlement and Immigration Policy Statement includes details on the terms of the immigration leave granted to individuals on the Afghan Citizens Resettlement Scheme. Leave granted through this scheme comes with recourse to public funds and individuals with this form of leave are eligible for DWP public funds benefits. Please refer to paragraph 33 (also pasted below).
33. Those resettled through the ACRS will receive fee-free indefinite leave to enter or remain in the UK, the right to work and immediate access to benefits if necessary.
